reconcile_note: The attacker-controlled group (cgiFormString -> acStack_64) and member (cgiFormString -> auStack_30a4) flow only into the callee at 0x0000a094, which is safe_system(0,0,"account","-m","-g",group,"-l",member,0). That callee packs its varargs into a discrete argv[] array and calls safe_exec, which fork()s and calls execvp(argv0, argv). No system/popen/"sh -c" is on this path, so group and member stay literal argv elements and shell metacharacters never reach a shell. The single raw system() call takes the fixed constant *0x00013788 = "makedav start & > /dev/null", with no attacker input. Everything else the function calls (FTP share setup at 0x00009db8, quota, xml/config writes, service restart) is off the command path. No user input reaches a shell, so the terminal is not-vulnerable. This verdict is auth-independent: the attacker input never reaches the shell, so it is not a command injection regardless of whether the path is authenticated. The upstream session check sym.check_login (0x22054) gates this handler, so the requested command runs only for a request that already holds a valid session.
